Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Computing & programming

user noun

of a computer, program or website

also users, computer user, end user, phone user

our formation

ūtēns, ūtentis m. or f.

present participle of ūtor, used as a noun

a user, one who uses

Our formation, the one the lexicon already uses in nōmen ūtentis (see username): no reference work has a word for a computer user. Classically the participle keeps its verb and takes the ablative (rēbus ūtentēs); as a noun it is clearest in the plural, ūtentēs, the people who use a program. Where a clause will do, Latin prefers the verb: quī hōc programmate ūtuntur, the users of this program.

Examples

  • Quot hominēs hōc programmate ūtuntur?

    How many users does this program have?composed

See also username, password, log in, computer, app, program.

SourcesLewis & Short: utor

No reference work (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi & Bini) has a word for a computer user.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
